title: Passive but accessible:  Studied information is not actively stored in working memory, yet attended regardless of anticipated load
description: This EEG study investigates how working memory accessibility is influenced by attentional expectations and prior learning. Participants performed a color-recall task with two memory screens containing studied and novel objects, while load expectations were manipulated across blocks. The dataset examines neural correlates of memory encoding and retrieval when information is passively accessible despite varying anticipated cognitive demands.
methods_description: EEG was recorded during a two-screen memory task with jittered intertrial intervals (600-1000 ms). The first screen (1000 ms) presented four objects (two to-be-memorized on one side, two balancing items on the opposite side), followed by a 1400 ms interstimulus interval. A second screen (1000 ms) presented additional novel items vertically around fixation. Load expectation was manipulated by varying the probability of second-screen items appearing (80% in high-load expectation, 20% in low-load expectation blocks). Participants performed color-recall responses on a continuous color wheel with corrective feedback for studied objects exceeding 40° error.
